The present invention relates to an elongated pelt board for accommodating an animal pelt. The pelt board comprises a first wall element, a second wall element being spaced apart from the first wall element in the first radial direction, a third wall element and a fourth wall element being spaced apart from the third wall element in a second radial direction. The invention relates to an elongated pelt board configured to receive and support an animal pelt. The pelt board includes four wall elements arranged in spaced pairs along respective first and second radial directions. Collectively, the wall elements define an internal cavity extending along the longitudinal direction of the board.

The wall elements are movable between a contracted state and an expanded state. In the contracted state, the radial distances between the wall elements are reduced, thereby decreasing the cross-sectional dimensions of the pelt board. In the expanded state, the radial distances are increased, enlarging the board’s cross-sectional dimensions to stretch and support the animal pelt.

An elongated core element is positioned within the cavity and is movable longitudinally relative to the wall elements. This longitudinal movement selectively displaces the wall elements between their contracted and expanded positions, thereby allowing the pelt board to be adjusted as required for fitting, stretching, drying, or removing the animal pelt.

The invention relates to an elongated pelt board for supporting and drying an animal pelt. The board comprises four longitudinally extending wall elements arranged around a central longitudinal axis and defining an internal cavity. Together, the wall elements form an outer supporting surface upon which the pelt may be positioned. At least some of the wall elements are radially movable so that the circumference or transverse dimensions of the board can be varied.

A movable core is disposed within the longitudinal cavity. The core is configured to move in the longitudinal direction relative to the wall elements and to cooperate with their inwardly facing surfaces. When the core is moved to a first longitudinal position, the wall elements are permitted or urged to move radially inward, placing the pelt board in a contracted state. In this state, the reduced transverse dimensions facilitate placement of a pelt on the board and removal of the pelt after drying or processing.

When the core is moved to a second longitudinal position, engagement between the core and the wall elements displaces at least some of the wall elements radially outward. The board is thereby brought into an expanded state in which the pelt is stretched and supported around the outer surfaces of the wall elements. The cooperating surfaces of the core and wall elements may be inclined, tapered, stepped, or otherwise shaped to convert longitudinal movement of the core into radial movement of the wall elements.

The core may be actuated manually or by a suitable mechanical drive and may include a locking or retaining arrangement for holding it in the selected position. By selectively moving the core between its first and second positions, an operator can quickly contract or expand the pelt board without having to dismantle it or forcibly pull the pelt over a fixed-width structure. The adjustable construction therefore improves the accommodation, stretching, drying, and handling of animal pelts while reducing the effort required to mount and remove them.

counterfactuals.output:
# Invention Disclosure

## Title

**Adjustable Animal-Pelt Drying Board with Axially Actuated Expansion Core**

## 1. Technical Field

The invention relates to devices for shaping, stretching, and drying animal pelts. More particularly, it concerns an adjustable pelt-drying board that selectively transitions between a contracted configuration and an expanded configuration through axial movement of an internal core.

## 2. Background

Traditional pelt-drying boards are generally rigid forms having a fixed width and thickness. A freshly prepared pelt is pulled over the board and secured while drying. Because animal pelts vary in size, fixed boards may require users to maintain multiple board sizes. A fixed board can also make it difficult to insert the board into a narrow pelt opening, uniformly tension the pelt, or remove the dried pelt without damage.

Existing adjustable forms may rely on separate wedges, exposed fasteners, inflatable components, or independently manipulated side members. Such arrangements can be cumbersome, produce uneven expansion, trap moisture, or create protrusions that mark or tear the pelt.

A need therefore exists for a drying board that is readily inserted in a contracted state, expands in a controlled and substantially uniform manner from an internal actuator, retains the selected configuration during drying, and contracts for convenient removal.

## 3. Summary of the Invention

The disclosed drying board includes:

- an elongated board assembly defining a longitudinal axis;
- a plurality of exterior pelt-supporting members arranged around an internal cavity;
- an internal core movable axially within the cavity; and
- one or more motion-conversion interfaces between the core and the exterior members.

Axial movement of the core in a first direction causes the exterior members to move outwardly, placing the board in an expanded configuration. Axial movement of the core in an opposite direction permits or causes the exterior members to move inwardly, placing the board in a contracted configuration.

The motion-conversion interfaces may include tapered surfaces, ramps, wedges, cams, inclined slots, linkages, or combinations thereof. A releasable locking mechanism may retain the core at one or more axial positions, thereby maintaining a selected board width, thickness, circumference, or cross-sectional profile.

The contracted configuration facilitates insertion into and removal from a pelt. The expanded configuration applies controlled outward tension to shape the pelt during drying.

## 4. Objectives and Advantages

The invention may provide one or more of the following advantages:

1. A single board can accommodate pelts of different sizes.
2. The board can be inserted and removed in a reduced-size configuration.
3. Expansion can be controlled from one end of the board.
4. The actuator and motion-conversion components can remain substantially enclosed.
5. Outward displacement can be distributed along much of the board length.
6. The pelt-contacting surface can remain smooth and free of exposed wedges or sharp hardware.
7. Drying ventilation can be provided through gaps, grooves, or apertures.
8. A repeatable expanded size can be selected using indexed locking positions.
9. The board can apply substantially symmetrical pelt tension.
10. Contraction can reduce the risk of damaging a dried pelt during removal.

## 5. General Construction

### 5.1 Exterior Pelt-Supporting Assembly

The exterior assembly may include two or more longitudinal support members, ribs, panels, slats, or shell segments. In one embodiment, the assembly includes:

- a left lateral member;
- a right lateral member;
- an anterior or upper member; and
- a posterior or lower member.

In a simpler embodiment, two opposed side members move laterally relative to a stationary central frame. In another embodiment, three, four, or more shell segments move radially outward.

The exterior members collectively define an elongated form corresponding generally to the shape of a desired dried pelt. The form may be tapered toward a nose end and wider toward a base end. Its cross section may be generally flat, oval, elliptical, circular, or species-specific.

The pelt-contacting surfaces are preferably smooth and may include rounded edges. Recessed channels, perforations, or spacing between adjacent members may promote airflow and moisture drainage.

### 5.2 Internal Cavity and Guide Structure

The exterior assembly defines an internal longitudinal cavity. The cavity receives the internal core and may include guide rails, bushings, sleeves, grooves, or bearing surfaces that constrain the core to substantially axial movement.

A central spine may support the exterior members and guide the core. Alternatively, the exterior members themselves may collectively define the guide passage.

### 5.3 Axially Movable Core

The internal core is an elongated actuator extending along at least part of the board. It may have a circular, polygonal, cruciform, or other cross-sectional shape selected to prevent unintended rotation or to permit controlled rotation where desired.

The core includes one or more actuator portions positioned to engage corresponding follower portions on the exterior members. An operating end of the core is accessible at the base or nose of the board. The operating end may include:

- a handle;
- a knob;
- a lever;
- a threaded adjustment member;
- a pull ring;
- a removable tool interface; or
- a foot or bench-operated actuator.

### 5.4 Motion-Conversion Interfaces

In one embodiment, the core carries a plurality of tapered cam sections. Each cam section increases in transverse dimension along the axial direction. Follower surfaces on the exterior members contact the cam sections. As the core moves axially toward the expanded position, the increasing transverse dimension forces the exterior members outward.

The cam sections may be spaced along the core to distribute expansion over the length of the board. The taper angles may differ from one location to another so that different portions of the board expand by different amounts. For example, a central or base portion may expand more than the tapered nose portion.

Suitable interfaces include:

- opposed wedge surfaces;
- conical or frustoconical core sections;
- inclined slots receiving follower pins;
- helical cam tracks;
- toggle links;
- articulated scissor links;
- rolling cam followers;
- eccentric surfaces; or
- resiliently deformable expansion elements.

Low-friction inserts, rollers, or wear-resistant coatings may be positioned between the core and followers.

### 5.5 Return or Contraction Mechanism

The exterior members may return inwardly when the core is retracted. Inward movement may be produced by:

- elastic bands positioned around the exterior members;
- tension or compression springs;
- flexible living hinges;
- resilient exterior members;
- inwardly acting linkages;
- a positive-drive cam slot that both expands and contracts the members; or
- tension exerted by the pelt before complete drying.

A positive-drive arrangement is preferred where controlled contraction is desired. In such an arrangement, pins attached to the exterior members travel in inclined slots formed in the core, so axial core movement positively drives the members both outward and inward.

### 5.6 Locking and Adjustment Mechanism

The core may be retained in a selected axial position by a lock. Suitable locks include:

- a spring-loaded detent engaging spaced recesses;
- a ratchet and pawl;
- a threaded collar;
- an over-center lever;
- a quarter-turn bayonet fitting;
- a cross pin;
- a friction clamp;
- a cam lock; or
- a continuously adjustable screw mechanism.

Indexed markings may identify board size or expansion amount. A force-limiting spring, slip clutch, torque-limited knob, or breakaway detent may prevent excessive pelt tension.

## 6. Exemplary Embodiment

An exemplary board has an elongated central frame with four longitudinal shell segments arranged around the frame. The shell segments form a generally oval exterior profile and are connected to the frame by transverse guide pins that permit limited radial movement.

An elongated core is slidably received within a central passage of the frame. The core includes three longitudinally spaced, frustoconical cam regions. Each shell segment includes inwardly directed followers aligned with the cam regions.

When the core is pulled toward the base end, larger-diameter portions of the cam regions move beneath the followers. The followers and corresponding shell segments are driven radially outward. Elastic retaining bands located in recessed circumferential channels urge the shell segments inward and maintain contact between the followers and cam regions.

A spring-loaded locking pin at the base end engages any of several apertures in the core. The apertures correspond to a contracted position and multiple expanded positions. The outer surface includes shallow longitudinal ventilation grooves and rounded interfaces between neighboring shell segments.

To contract the board, the user releases the locking pin and pushes the core toward the nose end. The smaller-diameter portions of the cam regions align with the followers, allowing the retaining bands to draw the shell segments inward.

## 7. Operation

A representative method of use includes:

1. Preparing the animal pelt for drying.
2. Releasing the core lock.
3. Moving the core axially to place the board in the contracted configuration.
4. Pulling the pelt over the contracted board.
5. Moving the core axially toward an expanded position.
6. Allowing the cam interfaces to displace the exterior members outward until the desired pelt tension or board dimension is reached.
7. Locking the core in the selected axial position.
8. Securing portions of the pelt to the board, if appropriate, and allowing the pelt to dry.
9. Releasing the lock after drying.
10. Moving the core in the opposite axial direction to contract the board.
11. Removing the dried pelt.

## 8. Alternative Embodiments

### 8.1 Two-Panel Board

The board may include two broad pelt-supporting panels that move apart in a thickness direction. The core may include opposed wedges that engage the interior surfaces of the panels.

### 8.2 Width-Only Expansion

A rigid central board may support two movable lateral edge rails. Axial movement of the core moves only the edge rails outward, increasing board width while maintaining substantially constant thickness.

### 8.3 Differential Expansion

The core may include independently shaped cam regions that produce greater expansion at the base than at the nose. This preserves a desired taper and prevents excessive stretching near narrower portions of the pelt.

### 8.4 Thread-Driven Core

The core may be axially displaced by rotating a threaded handle. Rotation of the handle advances or retracts the core relative to a threaded nut fixed to the frame. This configuration provides fine adjustment and self-locking operation.

### 8.5 Removable or Replaceable Shells

Interchangeable outer shell members may provide different lengths, tapers, surface textures, or species-specific profiles while using the same internal core and actuator assembly.

### 8.6 Segmented Longitudinal Expansion

Different exterior sections may be actuated sequentially. Multiple cam stages can first expand the central portion and subsequently expand the base or nose portion as the core moves farther axially.

### 8.7 Sealed Interior

Flexible seals or overlapping lips may cover gaps between shell segments to limit entry of fluids, tissue, salt, or debris into the internal mechanism while preserving exterior-member movement.

## 9. Materials and Manufacture

The exterior members may be formed from wood, polymer, fiber-reinforced composite, aluminum, stainless steel, or combinations thereof. Molded polymers may be selected for moisture resistance and ease of cleaning. The core and followers may be made from acetal, nylon, high-density polyethylene, aluminum, stainless steel, or other low-friction and corrosion-resistant materials.

Components may be machined, molded, extruded, stamped, laminated, or additively manufactured. Fasteners and springs are preferably corrosion resistant. Exterior surfaces may include antimicrobial, nonstick, or moisture-resistant coatings.

The device may be constructed so that the core can be removed for cleaning and maintenance.

## 10. Potential Inventive Features

Potentially protectable features include:

- axial movement of an internal core to expand and contract a pelt-drying board;
- multiple longitudinally spaced cam interfaces producing distributed expansion;
- differential cam profiles producing a predetermined changing cross section;
- an enclosed actuator that maintains a smooth exterior pelt-contacting surface;
- indexed axial core positions corresponding to different pelt sizes;
- positive-drive expansion and contraction through inclined slots and follower pins;
- force-limited expansion to avoid overstretching;
- independently replaceable exterior shell segments;
- a ventilation arrangement integrated with movable exterior members; and
- contraction of the board after drying to facilitate pelt removal.

## 11. Example Claim Concepts

1. **An adjustable animal-pelt drying apparatus comprising:** an elongated exterior assembly defining a longitudinal axis and an internal cavity; an internal core disposed within the cavity and movable along the longitudinal axis; and at least one motion-conversion interface coupling the core to a plurality of pelt-supporting members, wherein axial movement of the core causes the pelt-supporting members to move between contracted and expanded positions.

2. The apparatus of concept 1, wherein the motion-conversion interface includes at least one tapered cam surface.

3. The apparatus of concept 1, wherein the core includes multiple cam regions spaced along its length.

4. The apparatus of concept 3, wherein the cam regions produce different amounts of transverse displacement at different longitudinal locations.

5. The apparatus of concept 1, further comprising a releasable lock configured to retain the core in a selected axial position.

6. The apparatus of concept 5, wherein the lock provides multiple indexed expansion positions.

7. The apparatus of concept 1, further comprising a resilient return member urging the pelt-supporting members toward the contracted positions.

8. The apparatus of concept 1, wherein the motion-conversion interface positively drives the pelt-supporting members both outwardly and inwardly.

9. The apparatus of concept 1, wherein gaps or passages between the pelt-supporting members provide drying ventilation.

10. **A method of drying a pelt comprising:** placing an adjustable drying board in a contracted configuration by moving an internal core axially; positioning the pelt over the board; moving the internal core axially to displace exterior pelt-supporting members outwardly; locking the core in an expanded position while the pelt dries; and subsequently retracting the core to contract the board for removal of the dried pelt.

## 12. Abstract

An adjustable animal-pelt drying board includes an elongated exterior assembly having movable pelt-supporting members and an internal core movable along a longitudinal axis. Tapered cams, inclined slots, wedges, or other motion-conversion interfaces translate axial movement of the core into outward or inward movement of the pelt-supporting members. The board can therefore be contracted for insertion into or removal from a pelt and expanded to apply shaping tension during drying. A locking mechanism retains the core at one or more selected axial positions. Distributed or differently profiled cam regions may provide uniform or differential expansion along the board length.
